approach: The `athena` binary doubles as a `cargo` shim, as it already does for `pre-commit` and `commit-msg` (`main.rs:545-553`). For each producer invocation, `agent_spec` makes `<job_dir>/shim/cargo`, a symlink to the athena binary. It puts that directory first on the producer's PATH only. It also passes the slot settings in env vars, built and parsed by one `CargoShim` type in `athena-agent/src/env.rs`. When `main` sees argv[0] == `cargo`, it calls `slot_exec::run`. That finds the subcommand with a new `policy::cargo_subcommand`, which skips only flags in the now-`pub` `CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS`. For build, test, clippy and check it takes a `Class::Producer` slot from a `SlotQueue` over the shared slots dir. It then runs the real cargo, found on PATH minus the shim dir, and frees the slot when cargo exits. On `SlotWait` it prints `no build slot free for <limit> s; try again`, writes a wait note (`<job_dir>/slot-wait.json`) and exits 75 without starting cargo. The note read/write helpers go in `slots.rs`. In `producer_loop`, after a successful producer invocation, a note present means the producer's last cargo command gave up. The loop returns the `SlotWait` as an error. `produce_and_verify` turns it into `hold_for_slot_wait`, the same hold path as the disk gate before the producer (`mod.rs:1476-1477`). The job is recorded as `environment: build slot wait`, with no outcome and no attempt used. Retry fixes: register `athena-cli --test slot_exec` in `xtask/shard-timings.txt`, keep a fmt/metadata no-slot test, and have the criteria cite runnable commands.

decisions.choice: One binary dispatched on argv[0] == `cargo`, reached through a `<job_dir>/shim/cargo` symlink. This is not a `build-slot -- <cmd>` subcommand. The design doc is updated to say so.
decisions.reason: The producer types plain `cargo ...` and the policy checks it by name. Policy refuses a path-qualified program (`policy.rs:554-558`), so a subcommand would need a policy change. A PATH shim leaves the agent's command and the policy as they are. main.rs already dispatches on argv[0] for `pre-commit` and `commit-msg`. This is the candidate design of the earlier job, accepted in the reading.

rejected.option: A `build-slot -- <cmd>` subcommand as written in the design doc (section 6, step 4)
rejected.why: The agent would have to type it, and the policy would have to allow it and parse the inner command. That adds a second parser for cargo commands.

rejected.option: A shell script wrapper in the shim dir
rejected.why: A second file format. It would hold the slot with `flock` outside the SlotQueue, so no class order, ageing or SlotWait. The task and the repo rule say all code is Rust.

decisions.choice: Make `CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS` `pub` in policy.rs and add `pub fn cargo_subcommand(args: &[&str]) -> Option<&str>` beside it. It skips leading flags in the list and returns the first non-dash word. An unknown leading dash flag or no word gives `None`. `check_cargo` keeps its own loop, so its behavior and error text do not change. The wrapper takes no slot for `None`.
decisions.reason: One list, no copy (criterion 7). `cargo -q build` and `cargo --locked test` get the right subcommand. The policy already refuses unknown flags for agents, so `None` is only reached by a form the policy denies.

rejected.why: It would risk changing existing error text and behavior for no gain.

rejected.option: Copy the flag list into slot_exec.rs
rejected.why: Two lists drift. Criterion 7 forbids it.

rejected.option: Read only args[0] as the subcommand
rejected.why: This is the bug the criterion 2 test must catch: `cargo -q build` would take no slot.

decisions.choice: Slots are taken for build, test, clippy and check only. `fmt`, `metadata`, `tree`, `doc`, `run` and unknown forms run the real cargo directly with no slot.
decisions.reason: The brief names these four and the no-slot test for fmt and metadata. `run` and `doc` are allowed by the policy but are not in the brief's list, so they are left as they are today.

rejected.option: Also take a slot for `run` and `doc`
rejected.why: The brief does not ask for it. It is a one-line change in `CARGO_SLOT_SUBCOMMANDS` if wanted later.

decisions.choice: The host reads the wrapper's wait through a note file, `<job_dir>/slot-wait.json` (`SlotWait` JSON), with helpers in slots.rs: `wait_note_path`, `write_wait_note`, `read_wait_note`, `clear_wait_note`. The wrapper clears the note whenever it later gets a slot. `producer_loop` clears it before each producer invocation. After a Success outcome it returns the `SlotWait` as `Err`. `produce_and_verify` catches it and returns `Err(self.hold_for_slot_wait(ctx, closing, wait))`, since it still owns `closing`.
decisions.reason: The wrapper is a separate process inside the agent. A file under the job's own directory is the only channel, and slots.rs is already a deliverable. Returning an error reuses the hold path that the disk gate uses before the producer, and adds no `Flow` variant. A producer that retries and gets a slot is not held, because the note is cleared. A producer that gives up leaves its cargo commands unrun, so the job is held, not failed.

rejected.option: Only exit 75 and let the producer and verifier judge it
rejected.why: Criterion 3 needs the job recorded as held, not failed, and a verifier would see unbuilt work as a failure.
Every `match` on `Flow` in mod.rs would change.

rejected.option: Check the note also when the outcome is TimedOut or an error
rejected.why: Those paths close with kept work or a failure reason and are untouched. Holding would drop the kept candidate.

decisions.choice: The slot settings go in env vars set by `CargoShim::apply`. It is built in `agent_spec` from `jc.config.pipeline()` (`max_check_slots`, `build_wait_s`, `build_age_promote_s`), `self.state.slots_dir()` and the job dir, when `role == Role::Producer`. `env::build` and its `EnvSpec` are unchanged. The shim dir is prepended to PATH only on that path.
decisions.reason: `EnvSpec { .. }` is built in 11 places (run/mod.rs, run/checks.rs x2, introspect.rs, reading.rs, live.rs test, env.rs tests). Adding a field would touch them all. The verifier and checks keep the environment they have now (criterion 8). Both ends of the contract (set and read) live in env.rs.

rejected.why: It touches 11 constructors, and the checks' environments risk being changed.

rejected.option: Config read again by the wrapper from the repo
rejected.why: The wrapper runs in a snapshot with no athena.toml access. Passing the values is simpler.

decisions.choice: The real cargo is found on PATH with the shim dir removed. It runs with that stripped PATH and inherited stdio. The slot is held by the wrapper process for the child's lifetime, and the wrapper exits with the child's code (128+signal for a signal).
decisions.reason: A nested `cargo` that the real cargo or a test spawns would otherwise re-enter the shim and wait for a slot its parent holds, which deadlocks with one slot. The workspace sets `unsafe_code = "deny"`, so the wrapper cannot clear close-on-exec to `exec` and leave the lock fd with cargo. It waits instead.

rejected.option: exec the real cargo, keeping the lock fd
rejected.why: It needs fcntl, so `unsafe` or a new dependency.

rejected.option: Leave the shim on PATH for the child

decisions.reason: The fix for the earlier failure (`checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit`, ci_shards.rs:411-421, compares the file with the test units). The general check is a separate job.

risks.risk: A wrapper killed with SIGKILL could leave its child cargo running after the slot lock is freed, so more builds than slots run for a while. The workspace denies `unsafe`, so the lock fd cannot be passed to the child.
risks.mitigation: The Bash timeout and the kill switch end the agent's process group, which includes the child. The window is small. Not fixed here; named in the design doc.

risks.risk: A producer that gives up after a wait loses its run: the job is held and a later drain retries from the base, spending the producer's money again.
risks.mitigation: The hold is checked only when the note is still present after the final command, so a producer that retries and gets a slot is not held. The design doc says 'the producer may retry', and the wait is 1800 s.

risks.risk: A stale note from an earlier invocation could hold a job wrongly.
risks.mitigation: `producer_loop` clears the note before every producer invocation, and the wrapper clears it on any later successful slot. The core test covers retry after the note is gone.

risks.risk: The shim symlink could fail to be created, which would let the producer build with no slot.
risks.mitigation: `agent_spec` returns an error if `install` fails, so the producer does not start. Not silently ignored.

risks.risk: Timing-dependent tests could be flaky on a loaded CI machine.
risks.mitigation: The tests use file markers (`started-*`, `release-*`) and `queue.waiting()` polls with a 10 s bound, not fixed sleeps, as slots.rs tests do. The wait-limit test uses a 1 s wait.

risks.risk: `cargo run` and `cargo doc` stay outside the slot list although the policy allows them.
risks.mitigation: Matches the brief. The list is one constant and can be extended later.

risks.risk: Adding the test file unregistered fails the shard guard again, which was the earlier failure.
risks.mitigation: Step 10 adds the line, and criterion 5 runs the guard.

demonstrations.method: The integration test sets up a tempdir with a shim dir holding a symlink `cargo` to `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena")`. A second dir holds a fake `cargo` shell script. On start the script writes `started-<tag>`, waits for `release-<tag>`, then exits 0. Settings are one slot, a 30 s wait, and the slots dir of a real `SlotQueue` in a tempdir. The test starts producer process A (`cargo build`) and waits for `started-A`. It then starts process B and waits until `queue.waiting() == 1`. It asserts B has not written `started-B` and that `try_acquire()` is None. It releases A, then B starts, and it releases B. Last it asserts `try_acquire()` returns Some after both exit.
demonstrations.observes: While A holds the only slot, B is queued and has not run. After A's release B runs, and the slot is free once both are done.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the wrapper took no slot, B would write `started-B` while A held, and the `waiting() == 1` wait would time out. If the slot were not freed at exit, the final `try_acquire` would be None.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `slot_exec::run`, reached through the real `athena` binary run as `cargo` (argv[0] dispatch added in step 5). Fixtures: a real `SlotQueue` over a tempdir, and a fake cargo script on PATH after the shim dir. They are injected through the env vars `CargoShim::apply` builds. The fake only records and waits, so the slot logic is not in it. The seam is added by steps 3-5 and 9. The slot lock is real and test-created, and the test reads it with `SlotQueue::try_acquire`, which exists (slots.rs:168).

demonstrations.method: Same fixtures. With one slot, the test runs `cargo -q build` and then `cargo --locked test` through the shim. The fake cargo records its argv, writes `started`, and waits for `release`. At each `started` the test asserts `try_acquire()` is None. After the process exits it asserts `try_acquire()` is Some and that the fake got exactly the original argv. A unit test in athena-agent covers `cargo_subcommand(&["-q","build"]) == Some("build")`, `("--locked","test") == Some("test")`, and `None` for `["--config","x"]`.
demonstrations.observes: Both commands hold the slot while the fake runs and free it after, and the real cargo gets the arguments unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: A lookup of only args[0] sees `-q` or `--locked`, takes no slot, and `try_acquire` returns Some while the fake runs, which fails the assert.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `slot_exec::run` via the `athena` binary as `cargo`, and `athena_agent::policy::cargo_subcommand` (added in step 2). Fixtures as in criterion 1. The seam is added by steps 2-5.

demonstrations.method: In the cli test the settings are one slot and a 1 s wait. The test holds the slot with `try_acquire()` and runs `cargo build` through the shim. It asserts exit code 75 (not 0, 1 or 101). It asserts stderr equals `no build slot free for 1 s; try again`. It asserts the fake cargo's `started` file was never written, and that `slots::read_wait_note` on the note path returns the `SlotWait` with `limit_s == 1`. The core test uses the existing fake agent driver (`athena_with` and `counting(..)`, tests.rs:187, 2152). A script wrapped around `counting` runs when role is Producer. It writes the note with the production helper `crate::slots::write_wait_note` at the path given in `spec.env`, as the wrapper would. The test then calls `athena.go(..)`. It asserts the error downcasts to `SlotWait`, and the `held       environment: build slot wait` line was printed. It asserts the records show state Dispatched with no outcome and no score. It asserts `read_slot_hold` equals the wait, no resume mark exists, the verifier ran 0 times, and a retry after the note is gone runs the producer again and lands.

demonstrations.method: The diff shows `CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS` made `pub`, one new `cargo_subcommand` that reads it, and no change inside `check_cargo`. `crates/athena-cli/src/slot_exec.rs` calls `athena_agent::policy::cargo_subcommand` and has no flag literal list of its own. The existing policy tests run (`listed_git_and_cargo_commands_are_allowed` at policy.rs:1004, the denial cases near 1047) alongside the new `cargo_subcommand` unit test.
demonstrations.command: git diff -- crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs && cargo test --locked -p athena-agent policy
demonstrations.observes: One list. check_cargo behavior is unchanged and its tests pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: A second list in slot_exec.rs would show in the diff. A changed check_cargo would break its existing tests.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `check_cargo` (via `Policy::check`) and `cargo_subcommand`. Both are production code and no double is used. Step 2 adds the function.

demonstrations.method: The diff shows `build` and `EnvSpec` unchanged, with only `CargoShim` and its helpers added. The core test uses the fake driver. Its script records `spec.env` for the Producer and Verifier roles and for the checks' env. After `go` it asserts the producer's PATH starts with `<job_dir>/shim` and has the slot variables. It asserts the verifier's env has no shim dir and none of those variables, and PATH equals the parent's PATH.
demonstrations.command: git diff -- crates/athena-agent/src/env.rs && cargo test --locked -p athena-core only_the_producer_gets_the_cargo_shim_first_on_path
demonstrations.observes: Only the producer's PATH is changed. Verifier and check environments are as before.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the shim went on every role's PATH, or on the verifier's, the verifier assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `Athena::go`, then `agent_spec` and `producer_loop`. Double: the existing `FakeAgentDriver` script capturing `spec.env`. The capture is added by step 8, and the driver exists.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff's file list. `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry under [Unreleased] / Added that says producer cargo build, test, clippy and check take a build slot. The listed files do not include athena.toml, defaults.toml, any `.github/workflows` file, or anything under `records/`.
demonstrations.observes: The changelog entry is present. No governance file and no records path appears.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing entry or a touched governance file would show in the diff.
demonstrations.seam: The diff itself; no seam is needed. Step 11 writes the entry.
